points.description: States that a pointer holds, stores or contains the memory address (memory location) of another variable — wording such as 'it stores where another variable lives in memory', 'it contains the address of a variable' or 'it points to the memory location of another variable' earns the marks. Merely saying it 'points to something' or 'refers to a value' without any mention of a memory address does not earn full marks.
points.partial_credit: Half marks when the idea of an address/location in memory is present but it is not made clear that it is the address of another variable.

levels.says: Mentions memory address or memory location, but does not say whose address it is (e.g. 'it holds a memory address' or 'it points to a place in memory').
Only says it points to or refers to another variable/value, with no mention of a memory address or location.

points.description: States that a pointer is itself a variable (a variable in its own right, stored in memory), not just an address or a label. Any wording making clear the pointer is a variable earns the marks.
points.partial_credit: Half marks when the answer implies the pointer is a separate entity that holds something but does not call it a variable.

levels.says: Describes the pointer as something that holds or stores an address, without saying that it is itself a variable.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both ideas: a pointer is a variable, and what it holds is the memory address of another variable. Part marks are given when only one idea is present, or when the address idea is present but vague about being the address of another variable. An answer that only says a pointer 'points to' something, with no mention of a variable or a memory address, earns little or no credit.
